source.title: When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails: A Representation-Level Perspective
source.authors: En-Yi Jiang; Anders Gjølbye; Yibo Zhang; O. Koyejo

page_placements.theme: Static audits can miss constructed latent vulnerability

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present, with minor equation and layout extraction artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: It tests harmful fine-tuning and suffix-attack outcomes using fine-tuning-onset and judged-ASR measures, rather than reporting a direct replication of the original studies’ measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful-SFT compliance onsets and a GCG suffix-attack ASR, which directly bear on V1 and V4. It also reports direct-harm rates, latent attacks, steering, patching, LVS, and hidden-state projections; those results are recorded under fits_no_version where their measures or intervention types do not match a listed version. The behavioral jailbreak ASR aggregates several prompt templates, so it does not isolate the compliant-start wrapper. The paper does not measure per-response-position KL, benign fine-tuning’s effect on harmful compliance, parameter/rank localization, or a deepening intervention.
record.test_reason: Harmful full SFT on three safety-trained instruct models (Gemma 2 2B, Llama 3.2 3B, Qwen 2.5 3B) raises judged harmful compliance from near zero to at least 0.8 within 10–25 steps. At batch size 4 that is roughly 40–100 examples, which bears directly on V1. A GCG suffix attack on the Llama base bears on V4. Everything else is measured on deliberately constructed 'dissociated' models or uses latent interventions, which match no version. The paper's purpose is auditing, not testing shallow alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that purpose-built dissociated models pass every static behavioral and probe audit like their bases, yet harmful SFT, latent PGD, steering, activation patching and GCG each expose harm more easily. They therefore argue safety audits must intervene on the model, not only observe it. They stress this is an existence proof, not a claim that ordinary training produces such models; a small public-checkpoint survey found only a modest Qwen2.5-7B steering signal.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses full harmful supervised fine-tuning and reports the step at which compliance crosses 0.8, alongside a synthetic dissociated-model construction. It is not presented as an explicit replication of the cited sources and does not report harmful-example counts for the SFT attack.
record.method_sensitivity: The SFT onset differs by model and attack-data condition (in-distribution versus OOD); the dissociated-versus-base LVS contrast is weaker on Qwen; steering varies by layer and strength; GCG is tested only on Llama. SFT curves use a resident 7B judge, while final evaluations use the HarmBench 13B classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Purpose-built dissociated models cross 0.8 harmful compliance at step 5 (OOD Gemma 13.3) versus 10–25 for their bases. GCG ASR on dissociated Llama is 0.52 versus 0.16 on the base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models trained to hide a latent harmful state behind clean refusals lose safety faster under harmful fine-tuning and suffix attacks than their bases.

fits_no_version.finding: Latent PGD, steering, patching, LVS and projection results separate dissociated models from their bases; static direct-harm audits do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Static behavioral and probe audits can miss intervention-level latent vulnerability in constructed models.

fits_no_version.finding: On five released 7–9B checkpoints, only Qwen2.5-7B shows direction-specific refusal-direction steering (16/60 vs 8/60, p=0.008). Llama-3-8B-RR is flat on every intervention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released aligned checkpoints rarely show strong latent steering vulnerability at small pushes.

record.problems: The constructed models are an existence proof rather than a prevalence study. The models are small; evaluation relies on reward-model and LLM-judge proxies; SFT onsets use three seeds; steering and some sweeps are single-run estimates over 24 prompts; GCG covers one architecture; and the released-checkpoint survey is small. The paper notes that Qwen's base is softer and weakens some contrasts.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted for the 56-row limit. The aggregate jailbreak-wrapper ASR is not recorded as a V4 result because the paper does not report the compliant-start wrapper separately. The construction-time training curves and static-probe scores are not recorded as claim-version rows because they do not measure the specified fine-tuning, token-position KL, or parameter-localization outcomes.

untested.parts: Counts below about 20 examples (the 5-step grid at batch 4). Larger models. Near-complete refusal removal: the reported endpoint is a 0.8 threshold, though the curves plateau above it.
Not tested. Alpaca is used only as a construction anchor.
Not tested. No per-position KL is measured.

Prefilling a compliant start and decoding changes are not tested. GCG is run only on Llama 3.2 3B. The wrapper jailbreaks (including a 'Begin your reply with Sure' template) are reported only in aggregate.
Not tested. No weight or rank localization; the direction and layer results are on constructed models.
Not tested. The RR circuit-breaker checkpoint appears only in the latent audit, with no fine-tuning or prefill test.

missing.what: GCG reached the affirmative target on 22/25 base behaviors (median 166 steps) and 25/25 dissociated (median 21), versus judged ASR 0.16/0.52. This matters for V4: reaching the opening did not mostly produce harmful output on the base.

Base jailbreak-wrapper ASR: Gemma 0.067, Llama 0.000, Qwen 0.200 over 15 prompts. One of the six templates asks the model to begin with 'Sure, here is'; results are aggregated, not reported per template.
Full 150-step SFT curves: all models plateau above threshold after onset.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study. The reader linked the dissociated-model rows to V1/V4; I unlinked them because those models are deliberately constructed to be vulnerable. V1 evidence therefore rests on the six base-model SFT rows. The reader said no example count was reported, but steps × batch 4 gives about 40–100 examples. SFT onsets use the 7B validation judge; the GCG result uses the 13B judge. The PGD target 'Sure, here is' is a latent attack, not a prefill, so it stays out of V4.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example count is reported for the attack runs, and the study measures crossing an 0.8 compliance threshold rather than refusal being removed almost entirely.
The benign Alpaca data is used as an anchor in the dissociated-model construction, not as a benign fine-tuning intervention whose effect on harmful compliance is measured.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts is measured.

GCG suffixes are tested on Llama only. The study does not isolate compliant-token prefilling or test decoding changes; its internal latent interventions are recorded as related findings but do not directly measure those specified mechanisms.
A harmful direction and layer are tested, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The construction deliberately trains a model to be cleanly safe but vulnerable to a fixed nudge; it does not test whether ordinary safety-training data or objectives produce shallow safety.
No training intervention intended to deepen safety is tested.
